title: Head Start and Free School Lunch Elimination - Child Nutrition and Education Access Destruction
description_short: Head Start and Free School Lunch Elimination - Child Nutrition and Education Access Destruction
description_medium: Education and child-welfare groups describe Project 2025 proposals to cut public-school funding, Head Start and school-nutrition support. The linked sources do not establish that the administration eliminated Head Start, free school meals or the Community Eligibility Provision, or verify the draft’s figures for children affected. The proposed cuts and actual program status need to be distinguished.
description_long: The linked education and child-welfare groups discuss Project 2025 proposals affecting public-school funding, Head Start and nutrition assistance. Their material is relevant to the programs’ possible exposure to policy changes, but the supplied record does not identify an enacted order, grant cancellation or statutory change that eliminated the programs. It also does not support the draft’s claims that Head Start was ended, that universal free meals disappeared, or that nearly 20 million students lost Community Eligibility Provision support. Those are described as completed outcomes in the original long text, although the available sources are about proposals. Head Start provides early-childhood services, while school meal programs and the Community Eligibility Provision help schools serve meals without collecting household applications from each participating family. To report actual effects, the record needs program-by-program funding and eligibility decisions, dates, and reliable figures on students or sites affected. On the current evidence, the subject is a proposed policy direction and the uncertainty around implementation, not a documented nationwide elimination.

title: Trump: Ukrainian intelligence is recorded admitting Mogilevich's ties to Putin
description_short: Trump: Ukrainian intelligence is recorded admitting Mogilevich's ties to Putin
description_medium: TrumpFile attributes to a published transcript a private conversation between Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and former security chief Leonid Derkach, recorded by Mykola Melnychenko. In the exchange, Derkach says Semion Mogilevich had been in contact with Vladimir Putin since Putin lived in Leningrad. The packet does not connect this recording to Donald Trump.
description_long: The linked TrumpFile page describes a private meeting between Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and former head of the Ukrainian security service Leonid Derkach. It says Kuchma’s security detail, including Mykola Melnychenko, recorded the conversation. In the excerpt, Kuchma asks whether Derkach has found Semion Mogilevich and whether they are working together. Derkach replies that Mogilevich is on good terms with Vladimir Putin and that the two had been in contact since Putin was still in Leningrad. TrumpFile says journalist J.V. Koshiw obtained the transcript and published it in his book, *The Politics of Kuchma – the Melnychenko Recordings, August 1999 to September 2000*, and links to a Jamestown analysis of Mogilevich and Putin. These are claims attributed to a transcript and secondary references; the packet does not independently verify the recording or transcript’s authenticity. It also supplies no evidence tying the conversation or its participants to Donald Trump, despite the title’s Trump framing.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Ukrainian intelligence is recorded admitting Mogilevich's ties to Putin
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Ukrainian intelligence is recorded admitting Mogilevich's ties to Putin

notes: The linked timeline identifies the attributed speakers, recorder, transcript book and a Jamestown reference, but says the authenticity of the recording was not independently verified. The excerpt does not connect the recording or its claims about Semion Mogilevich and Vladimir Putin to Donald Trump. An authenticated recording and a source establishing the Trump connection are needed to support the title.

title: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
description_short: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
description_medium: Reuters reported that El Salvador’s president offered to accept deportees from the United States in the country’s prisons. The supplied record expands that report into a claim that the United States made a deal to send American citizens to CECOT, but it does not establish a signed agreement, transfer authority or any transfer of a U.S. citizen. The offer and the claimed arrangement must be distinguished.
description_long: A Reuters report linked to this record said El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele offered to house people deported from the United States in Salvadoran prisons. The article described a proposal amid discussions between Bukele and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio about migration enforcement. An offer to accept deportees is different from a completed agreement, a lawful transfer of a U.S. citizen, or an actual deportation to a foreign prison. The supplied record does not include a signed arrangement, identify authority for transferring American citizens, or show that any U.S. citizen was sent to El Salvador. It also does not establish that CECOT was an agreed destination for American prisoners. The headline’s claim that the United States “makes deal” to deport Americans therefore exceeds the linked report as summarized here. A formal agreement, agency guidance or documented transfer would be needed to describe the legal terms and practical outcome. Until then, this account can report the public offer and the unresolved questions about whether the proposal became policy.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison

notes: The Reuters and AP summaries support a public offer to house U.S. deportees, but not a signed agreement, an agreed CECOT destination for Americans, transfer authority, or any transfer. The title's claim of a completed deal is unsupported; the description separates the offer from an implemented arrangement.

title: DOJ Released 1,000+ Trump Mentions from Suppressed Epstein Files
description_short: DOJ Released 1,000+ Trump Mentions from Suppressed Epstein Files
description_medium: A February 2026 PBS NewsHour interview summarized an NPR investigation alleging that the Justice Department withheld Epstein-related records containing allegations involving Donald Trump. The segment described a heavily redacted FBI interview and said the White House denied the underlying allegation. It does not establish the title’s claim of more than 1,000 released Trump mentions or the full release chronology.
description_long: PBS NewsHour discussed an NPR investigation on February 24, 2026, reporting that the Justice Department had withheld some Epstein-related records containing allegations involving President Donald Trump. Miami Herald reporter Julie K. Brown said an FBI interview with a woman who alleged she was assaulted by Trump when she was 13 appeared in released files but was heavily redacted, making it difficult to know what she told investigators. Brown described how an independent journalist compared report numbers and Bates stamps with records previously produced to Ghislaine Maxwell’s defense. Democrats on the House Oversight Committee said withholding the files could be unlawful. The White House denied the underlying allegation. The segment raised questions about redactions and missing records but did not present the interview report or establish why particular pages were withheld. It also does not substantiate the title’s count of more than 1,000 Trump mentions, a March 5 release, or the specific email and interview details in the supplied synopsis.

preserved_fields.title: DOJ Released 1,000+ Trump Mentions from Suppressed Epstein Files
preserved_fields.description_short: DOJ Released 1,000+ Trump Mentions from Suppressed Epstein Files

notes: Needs context: the PBS transcript supports an NPR report about withheld, heavily redacted records and an allegation denied by the White House. It does not substantiate the title’s 1,000-plus count, March release sequence, specific email, or the underlying interview details.
